subject: Defining SKUs, regions and co-sell approach for AWS / Azure / GCP listings
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: aws-marketplace-partner@amazon.com, azure-partners@microsoft.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: SKU / region strategy — initial matrix and ask

Team — attaching the latest "marketplace_sku_matrix_v3.xlsx" and want a quick sync on how we should list across AWS, Azure, and GCP. High-level asks:

- Should we keep the SAME packaging names (e.g., Starter / Business / Enterprise) across clouds or adapt names per cloud?
- Which regions do we target for launch per cloud (minimal footprint to enable co-sell vs broader coverage)?
- Billing model per cloud: subscription-only vs support for metered usage (AWS allows both; Azure prefers transactable offers for co-sell; GCP has nuances).

Options I sketched in the sheet:
A) Unified taxonomy + per-cloud SKU suffix (recommended by partnerships) — single feature buckets, different SKU codes per marketplace.
B) Cloud-specific bundles that map to local partner incentives (more work, easier for cloud reps in some cases).
C) Minimal initial footprint (US/EU on AWS+Azure) and GCP delayed to v2.

Constraints we know:
- Azure co-sell workflows want transactable offers and associated MSFT onboarding.
- AWS supports SaaS subscriptions + private offers + metered billing; metered needs agent integration.
- GCP listings require special onboarding and can be slower to approve.

Please reply with a short vote (A/B/C) and any blockers. If you have specific region lists, paste them inline. I want to finalize the SKU names and region flags by EOD 12 Feb so we can hand to cloud partners for intake.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0132

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU / region strategy — initial matrix and ask

On Tue, Feb 10, 2026 at 4:12 PM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — attaching the latest "marketplace_sku_matrix_v3.xlsx" and want a quick sync on how we should list across AWS, Azure, and GCP.

Quick take — vote A (Unified taxonomy) with these clarifications:
- Keep packaging names identical (Starter / Business / Enterprise) for marketing and doc parity.
- Use per-cloud SKU codes (e.g., RWD-STARTER-AWS, RWD-STARTER-AZR, RWD-STARTER-GCP) so billing/ledgering is clean.
- Region rollout: prioritize AWS + Azure in US & EU simultaneously so we can enable co-sell motions in both clouds quickly. GCP = v2 (target APAC + additional EU regions).

Notes / blockers:
- Need product confirmation on metering: if we want metered token billing on AWS at launch, infra needs time to instrument meter collection. That affects timeline and whether we default to subscription-only initially.
- Finance needs to sign off on list vs net pricing bands; any cloud-specific mandatory discounts for co-sell must be encoded in the pricing spreadsheet.

Action: I'll sync with Finance this afternoon; Ben, can you add the SKU suffix column and the proposed launch region flags in the sheet? I'll own pricing bands and discount rules.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, azure-partners@microsoft.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU / region strategy — initial matrix and ask

Ben / all — thanks for the clear framing. A couple of procurement/legal items that will materially affect execution:

1) Azure co-sell: MS requires an approved transactable offer and partner onboarding (publisher profile, offer listing). There are specific terms around data residency for some enterprise customers. If we target West Europe and East US, ensure the offer metadata reflects those regions and that we have the proper commercial contact set up with MS.

2) AWS marketplace: two main listing types for SaaS — Listing as SaaS (subscription) vs. Private Offers / AMI. Metered billing is supported but requires a metering service and reconciliation. If we plan to support token-based metering on day 1, expect an extra ~4-6 weeks for integrations and testing.

3) GCP: approvals are stricter for visibility (they vet pricing/usage patterns). If we want GCP co-sell, prepare for a lead time similar to Azure or longer, and expect to provide a SOC2 summary and a short security checklist (I've attached a draft checklist).

4) Contractual nuances: do not promise feature parity across listings in the public offer docs if we plan to enable region-specific features (callouts cause confusion and procurement pushback). Use "availability by region" table instead.

I've attached "azure_co-sell_guidelines.pdf" and a short GCP checklist. If everyone agrees on unified packaging + per-cloud SKU suffixes, Legal/Procurement will prepare a short compliance checklist for each cloud's intake.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal & Procurement, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SKU / region strategy — initial matrix and ask

Thanks everyone — summary and decisions to move forward: (finalize by EOD 12 Feb)

Decisions
- Packaging: Adopt unified names across clouds: Starter / Business / Enterprise. (Rationale: marketing + doc consistency)
- SKU format: Use a shared canonical SKU with cloud suffix: <RWD>-<PACK>-<CLOUD> (e.g., RWD-ENT-AWS). Karthik will produce the SKU code list.
- Billing model at launch: Subscription-only for Starter & Business across all clouds. Enterprise will have an opt-in metered add-on on AWS only for first release (metering to be gated by infra readiness).
- Regions for initial listing:
  * AWS: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1
  * Azure: East US, West Europe
  * GCP: us-central1, europe-west1 (APAC to follow in Q2)

Action items (owner / due)
- Ben: Update "marketplace_sku_matrix_v3.xlsx" with SKU codes and region flags (due 12 Feb EOD) — OWNER: ben_carter
- Karthik: Finalize pricing bands + write discount rules for co-sell (due 13 Feb) — OWNER: karthik_iyer
- Jonas: Prepare cloud intake checklist and confirm doc packages for MSFT/AWS/GCP (due 16 Feb) — OWNER: jonas_weber
- Marissa: Coordinate intake meetings with AWS Marketplace and Azure partner rep, schedule co-sell enablement sessions (due 18 Feb) — OWNER: marissa_cole

Ben — once you update the sheet I will consolidate and push to the cloud partner intake trackers and loop in the partner contacts (cc'd earlier). Good call to keep GCP for a short delay so we can focus on AWS+Azure co-sell motion.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
